repositories.brief_summary: New `Sys.filepath_exists`, hardened bytecode loading, and native FMA/sqrt codegen for arm64, power, riscv and s390x landed on trunk.
repositories.new_features_summary: `Sys.filepath_exists` added, bytecode TOC-overflow guard, and native FMA/sqrt/byte-swap instructions on multiple architectures.
repositories.new_features:
- Added `Sys.filepath_exists`, a stricter alternative to `Sys.file_exists` that reports permission and other system errors via a `Sys_error` exception instead of silently returning `false`, and clarified the documentation of `file_exists` to recommend the new function ([#14974](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14974), [#12393](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/12393)) by [Khalid](https://github.com/khalidbelk).
- Hardened bytecode executable loading in `caml_read_section_descriptors` against overflow when a corrupted or malicious file declares 2^29 or more table-of-contents entries ([#14872](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14872)) by [Xavier Leroy](https://github.com/xavierleroy).
- `Float.fma` now emits a native fused multiply-add instruction on arm64, power, riscv and s390x instead of calling into C ([#15008](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15008)) by [Zane Hambly](https://github.com/Zaneham).
- The s390x backend now emits `sqdbr` for square root and `lrvgr`/`lrvr` for byte swap natively rather than going through C ([#15002](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15002)) by [Zane Hambly](https://github.com/Zaneham).
- The riscv backend now emits `fsqrt.d` for square root natively ([#15005](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15005)) by [Zane Hambly](https://github.com/Zaneham).
- 32-bit builds now default to and recommend large-file (LFS) and year-2038-safe `time_t` support via `configure`, with `--disable-largefile` and `--disable-year2038` available to opt out ([#14997](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14997)) by [Antonin Décimo](https://github.com/MisterDA).
- Added a cross-backend testsuite check for `sqrt` covering zeros, infinities, NaN, denormals and exact squares, pinning behaviour used by the s390x and riscv sqrt changes ([#15007](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15007)) by [Zane Hambly](https://github.com/Zaneham).
repositories.activity_summary: Five PRs opened this week target runtime-events corrupt-stream bugs and architecture codegen, alongside ongoing minor-GC and native-atomics work.
repositories.activity:
- Five newly opened PRs remain unmerged: native rounding instructions (`Float.round`, `trunc`, `ceil`, `floor`) for arm64 and power ([#15017](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15017)) by [Zane Hambly](https://github.com/Zaneham); a fix for the `runtime_events` "corrupt stream" failure that adds a producer-side memory fence and consumer re-check, with detailed reproduction data across amd64, arm64, riscv64 and ppc64le ([#15016](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15016)) by [Tim McGilchrist](https://github.com/tmcgilchrist); an earlier, narrower fix for the same corrupt-stream issue ([#15015](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15015)) by [Sadiq Jaffer](https://github.com/sadiqj), which the two authors are now discussing combining; widening `lost_words` from `int` to `uint64_t` in the runtime-events lost-events callback to avoid wraparound past `INT_MAX` ([#15010](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15010)) by [Tim McGilchrist](https://github.com/tmcgilchrist); and physical-equality fast paths for `Set.union`, `Set.inter` and `Set.diff` that improve complexity for sets with structural sharing, carried internally at LexiFi for over a decade ([#15009](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15009)) by [Nicolás Ojeda Bär](https://github.com/nojb).
- The `runtime_events` subsystem received concentrated attention beyond the corrupt-stream PRs: a `size_t` fix for ring-buffer file-size overflow past 2 GiB ([#15000](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15000), fixing [#14999](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14999)) and a proposal to expose `EV_C_MAJOR_DIRECT_ALLOCATED_WORDS` and related direct/suspended/resume counters ([#15001](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15001)), both by [Tim McGilchrist](https://github.com/tmcgilchrist), remain open.
- The minor-GC rewrite that inlines the `oldify_one` fast path and upstreams work from OxCaml continues under review, with [Eduardo Souza](https://github.com/udesou) publishing a benchmarking dashboard showing mostly improvements with one workload regression tied to glibc malloc tuning ([#14571](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14571)) by [Nick Barnes](https://github.com/NickBarnes).
- Native atomic exchange and compare-and-set generation across all architectures, follow-up to the fetch-and-add work, remains open for review with a call for extra eyes on the riscv and power fences ([#14980](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14980)) by [Zane Hambly](https://github.com/Zaneham).
- Type-checker cleanup continues in draft form: removing an unnecessary `unify_var` call in `enforce_current_level` ([#14995](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14995)) and making abstract types defined directly in structures injective, a follow-up to [#14982](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14982) and [#14990](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14990) ([#14991](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14991)), both by [Jacques Garrigue](https://github.com/garrigue).
- [Jeremy Yallop](https://github.com/yallop) proposed fixing `Weak.get_copy` so it no longer shallow-duplicates continuations, which can otherwise crash a program with a segmentation fault ([#14988](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14988)).
- Build and CI work continued from [Antonin Décimo](https://github.com/MisterDA): enabling KVM for hardware-accelerated Android emulation in CI, saving roughly 40 seconds per job ([#15003](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15003)), and switching `configure` to Autoconf's own C++ compiler detection to fix a `-std=gnu23` build failure ([#14996](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14996)).
repositories.discussions_summary: Detailed cross-platform debugging of the runtime-events corrupt-stream bug and the Sys.filepath_exists documentation wording dominated discussion.
repositories.notable_discussions:
- The `runtime_events` "corrupt stream" bug ([#14151](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14151)) prompted parallel investigation: [Sadiq Jaffer](https://github.com/sadiqj) proposed a consumer-side re-check ([#15015](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15015)), while [Tim McGilchrist](https://github.com/tmcgilchrist) traced a second, independent cause — a release-store ordering bug in `write_to_ring` — and added a producer-side fence ([#15016](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15016)); [Zane Hambly](https://github.com/Zaneham) independently reproduced the failure on riscv64 and confirmed the combined fix eliminates it while the consumer-only fix does not.
- Wording for the new `Sys.filepath_exists` and revised `Sys.file_exists` documentation went through several rounds between [Xavier Leroy](https://github.com/xavierleroy), [Daniel Bünzli](https://github.com/dbuenzli) and [Khalid](https://github.com/khalidbelk), settling on plain-language phrasing that avoids POSIX-specific terms like `stat`, `ENOTDIR` and `ENOENT` since `Sys` module readers are not assumed to know POSIX systems programming ([#14974](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14974)).
- [Jeremy Yallop](https://github.com/yallop) found that `Weak.get_copy` shallow-duplicates effect-handler continuations, producing two continuations sharing one fiber and causing a segmentation fault when both are resumed ([#14988](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14988)).
- [Ryan Tjoa](https://github.com/rtjoa) reported that `[%atomic.loc]` on a polymorphic mutable record field can be used to implement `Obj.magic`, an unsoundness hole credited in part to a discussion with Nathan Farlow ([#14987](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14987)).
- Whether `runtime_events` constructor indices should be covered by a maintained wire-format version field was debated by [Gabriel Scherer](https://github.com/gasche), [Sadiq Jaffer](https://github.com/sadiqj), [Tim McGilchrist](https://github.com/tmcgilchrist) and [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm), converging on bumping the version now and enforcing an append-only policy for constructors going forward ([#15011](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15011)).
- Reviewers debated whether the new sharing-based fast paths in `Set.union`/`inter`/`diff` warrant documenting the resulting complexity guarantees, with [Vincent Laviron](https://github.com/lthls) and [Daniel Bünzli](https://github.com/dbuenzli) leaning toward leaving the documentation unchanged since the guarantee is not simple to state precisely ([#15009](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15009)).
- [Vincent Laviron](https://github.com/lthls) found that the ocamldebug wire protocol clamps object headers to 32 bits, which can silently truncate large array sizes during remote debugging, surfaced while investigating support for the Introcaml tool ([#15012](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15012)).
- [Tim McGilchrist](https://github.com/tmcgilchrist) and [Zane Hambly](https://github.com/Zaneham) confirmed the flambda+ThreadSanitizer test combination fails on ppc64le, amd64 Linux and arm64 macOS due to flambda's anonymous-function symbol naming and missing race reports, with McGilchrist taking on the fix ([#15014](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15014)).
repositories.trends_summary: Continued native-codegen work across non-amd64 backends and a cluster of runtime_events correctness fixes surfaced in the same week.
repositories.emerging_trends:
- Systematic replacement of C-call fallbacks with native instructions on arm64, power, riscv and s390x continues, covering FMA, square root, byte swap and now rounding operations, largely driven by [Zane Hambly](https://github.com/Zaneham) ([#14980](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14980), [#15002](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15002), [#15005](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15005), [#15006](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15006), [#15008](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15008), [#15017](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15017)).
- Several independent integer-overflow and correctness bugs in `runtime_events` were reported and fixed in the same period — ring-buffer size overflow, `lost_words` truncation, constructor-index versioning and the corrupt-stream race — indicating active hardening of that subsystem by [Tim McGilchrist](https://github.com/tmcgilchrist) and [Sadiq Jaffer](https://github.com/sadiqj) ([#14999](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14999), [#15000](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15000), [#15001](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15001), [#15010](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15010), [#15011](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15011), [#15015](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15015), [#15016](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15016)).
- Build-system modernization keeps moving toward standard Autoconf idioms rather than hand-rolled checks, for large-file/year-2038 support and C++ compiler detection ([#14997](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14997), [#14996](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14996)) by [Antonin Décimo](https://github.com/MisterDA).

repositories.brief_summary: opam 2.6.0~beta1 was released, bundling switch-list repair, safe-mode fixes, and git gc/maintenance hardening.
repositories.new_features_summary: opam 2.6.0~beta1 ships reinit switch-list repair, safe-mode cache/debug fixes, and disabled git gc/maintenance on managed repositories.
repositories.new_features:
- `opam init --reinit` now regenerates the list of valid switches and repairs internal switch metadata (cache, config, packages) instead of leaving stale entries behind [#7068](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7068)
- opam disables `gc.autoDetach` and `maintenance.autoDetach` via `git config --local` on every repository it manages, preventing a detached git maintenance job from racing opam's own removal of build directories [#7073](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7073)
- Safe mode (`--safe`) now respects an outdated cache file instead of silently rewriting it, and no longer forces `debug-level` back to `0` when combined with `--debug` [#7067](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7067), [#7091](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7091)
- `OpamStd.Env` gained a `raw = string array` type alias plus `get_from_array` and `add_and_replace` helpers, and `opamGit.ml` was switched to build its `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT`/`GIT_CONFIG_KEY_*`/`GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_*` environment through them rather than a hand-built array, fixing undefined behaviour from duplicate environment keys per POSIX.1-2024 [#7073](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7073)
- `OpamGlobalState.load` and `fix_switch_list` now log (at debug level 4) which switches were dropped when repairing an inconsistent switch list, instead of silently rewriting the config [#7068](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7068)
- opam 2.6.0~beta1 was tagged and published with signed binaries for Linux, macOS and Windows across multiple architectures, alongside updated install scripts referencing the new version [#7095](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7095), [#7099](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7099)

repositories.discussions_summary: Discussion continued on GC tuning trade-offs on low-end hardware and OpenBSD's per-architecture compiler toolchain for static linking.
repositories.notable_discussions:
- [Gabriel Scherer](https://github.com/gasche) and [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate) discussed benchmarking results on [#7100](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7100), exploring whether tuning `OCAMLRUNPARAM` space-overhead or forcing manual `Gc.compact`/`full_major` reduces opam's memory footprint on low-end hardware, noting OCaml 5.x does not release memory to the OS without explicit compaction
- [Sebastien Marie](https://github.com/semarie) clarified OpenBSD's per-architecture compiler toolchain (which architectures use `gcc` vs `clang`) in response to [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate)'s static-linking work, helping confirm the `--enable-static` change is safe for OCaml's supported native backends ([#6705](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6705))
- [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate) linked the git fsmonitor socket failure in `repository set-url` ([#7054](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7054)) to the broader git-maintenance race condition tracked in [#7031](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7031), noting [#7073](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7073) only partially addresses the category and leaving it open for further work

repositories.brief_summary: New `dune ocaml inferred-mli` command and Landlock sandboxing landed alongside a breaking context-name restriction.
repositories.new_features_summary: New `dune ocaml inferred-mli` command, Landlock sandboxing, describe-workspace module origins, and a breaking context-name restriction.
repositories.new_features:
- New `dune ocaml inferred-mli MODULE` command infers an OCaml interface using the module's actual build configuration (preprocessing, dependencies, opens, parameter flags) and reports it through Dune's promotion workflow so it can be applied with `dune promote` ([#16111](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16111), fixes [#12727](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/12727), [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg))
- Sandboxed actions on Linux with Landlock ABI 3+ are now confined from writing outside the action sandbox, temporary directory, action-trace directory, and `/dev`, starting with Dune language 3.25; opt out with `DUNE_CONFIG__LANDLOCK=disabled` ([#15858](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15858), [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg))
- **BREAKING CHANGE:** context names may no longer contain `:` so they remain portable path components on Windows and Cygwin, alongside the existing `/` and `\` restriction ([#16085](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16085), [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg))
- `dune describe workspace` now reports an `origin` for every module — `source` (hand-written), `dune` (generated by a `rule` stanza, pointing at the generating file), `ocamllex`/`ocamlyacc`/`menhir`, or `wrapper` (synthesised by Dune) — with new `--with-origin-deps` and `--with-origin-deps-expanded` flags reporting a rule-generated module's declared and expanded dependencies ([#15478](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15478), [Nat Karmios](https://github.com/nat-karmios))
- `dune pkg lock` now fails without writing a lock directory if any platform requested by `solve_for_platforms` cannot be solved, instead of silently producing a partial lock directory ([#15981](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15981), [Ali Caglayan](https://github.com/Alizter))
- Fixed a crash generating install rules for a Melange-only implementation of an installed virtual library ([#16033](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16033), [Antonio Nuno Monteiro](https://github.com/anmonteiro))
- Fixed Merlin definition lookup for libraries with private modules ([#15977](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15977), fixes [#4892](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/4892), [Antonio Nuno Monteiro](https://github.com/anmonteiro))
- Fixed native OCaml plugins (`.cmxs`) going missing from package layouts used when compiling Rocq theories, by materializing `Libexec` entries alongside `Lib` ([#16054](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16054), [Ali Caglayan](https://github.com/Alizter))
- Fixed watch mode remaining stale after the file-watcher event queue overflows ([#16068](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16068), fixes [#16052](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16052), [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg))
- Fixed a crash where build cancellation on macOS could raise `EPERM` while signaling a process group ([#16059](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16059), fixes [#16053](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16053), [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg))
- Generated MDX executables now inherit `link_flags` from `env` stanzas ([#15614](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15614), fixes [#15613](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15613), [@copilot-swe-agent](https://github.com/copilot-swe-agent), reviewed by [Ali Caglayan](https://github.com/Alizter))
- `dune ocaml top-module`, `dune ocaml top`, promotion commands, and `dune describe workspace` now all correctly accept absolute directory/source paths and paths relative to a workspace subdirectory, rather than only paths relative to the workspace root ([#16135](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16135), [#16142](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16142), [#16143](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16143), [#16144](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16144), [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg))
- `dune pkg outdated` now fails early with a clear message when package management is not enabled, instead of a confusing error ([#16065](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16065), [Shon Feder](https://github.com/shonfeder))
- Fixed a memory-table invalidation bug where nodes could be cleared before being invalidated ([#16068](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16068), [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg))
- A round of performance work targeted the build engine and standard library internals: reusing parsed transitive dependencies and identical rule maps ([#15963](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15963), [#15915](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15915)), preserving unchanged target sets and avoiding intermediate validation states ([#16069](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16069), [#16078](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16078), [#16101](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16101)), a more compact Blake3 digest representation ([#16100](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16100)), and batched qualified-module dependency lookups ([#15752](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15752), [#16087](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16087)) by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg) and [Antonio Nuno Monteiro](https://github.com/anmonteiro)
- Documentation for the `For_rocq_only` install-layout escape hatch was updated to reflect that it now also covers `Section.Libexec` entries, matching the opam-style `lib/<package>` layout ([14665cb](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/commit/14665cb6dbe61c9b92c8369145f8c7ae812ca47f))

repositories.discussions_summary: Users flagged shared-cache correctness issues on macOS and limits in dune exec's runtime dependency handling for sites.
repositories.notable_discussions:
- [Thomas Gazagnaire](https://github.com/samoht) reported that the shared cache misses when the build directory is named by its absolute path ([#16072](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16072)) and that a cram test writing to one of its own files mutates the shared cache entry for that content; [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg) noted existing Linux workarounds via bwrap/Landlock don't extend to macOS, and [Ali Caglayan](https://github.com/Alizter) suggested macOS's copy-on-write `clonefile` as a possible fix ([#16077](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16077))
- [Thomas Gazagnaire](https://github.com/samoht) also reported that editing a `(private_modules ...)` interface doesn't trigger a consumer rebuild, later failing with an "inconsistent assumptions over interface" error ([#16071](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16071))
- [Rodolphe Lepigre](https://github.com/rlepigre-skylabs-ai) raised difficulty making a library depend on a binary at runtime; [Ali Caglayan](https://github.com/Alizter) and [Jan-Oliver Kaiser](https://github.com/Janno) discussed `%{bin:...}` expansion limits, the under-maintained sites plugin, and the lack of a way for `dune exec` to declare a runtime dependency ([#16050](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16050))

repositories.brief_summary: Package archival triage, OCaml 5.5 compatibility bounds, and security-driven releases of cohttp, eio and mirage-crypto.
repositories.new_features_summary: cohttp fixed a path-traversal bug, mirage-crypto fixed a timing leak, eio gained Windows paths, and several new packages landed.
repositories.new_features:
- `cohttp` 6.3.0 fixes a **path-traversal vulnerability** in `Cohttp.Path.resolve_local_file`, which no longer escapes the docroot on percent-encoded `..%2f` sequences, and adds `Cohttp.Path.normalise` for servers to safely inspect request path segments before making access-control decisions, released by [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) ([#30528](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30528))
- `mirage-crypto` 2.4.0 fixes a **timing leak** in elliptic-curve lookup tables (OSEC-2026-17, reported by torinnd) alongside a hardcoded Diffie-Hellman group fix, released by [Hannes Mehnert](https://github.com/hannesm) ([#30507](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30507))
- `eio` 1.5 adds **Windows path support** so `Eio.Path.t` no longer assumes POSIX-style separators, plus pre-connect socket options (`?bind_to`, `?options`) on `Eio.Net.connect` and a new `Eio.Path.of_dir` convenience, by [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) and [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) ([#30518](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30518))
- `prometheus` 2.0 splits the client library into a new `prometheus-eio` serving package and a cohttp-free `prometheus-reporter`, removes Lwt from the core registry, and lets `--listen-prometheus` bind `tcp:HOST[:PORT]` or `unix:PATH` addresses, by [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) ([#30535](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30535))
- `cascade` 1.1.0 ships breaking changes to the CSS engine — `Css.hex` now raises on malformed input, `Apply.Make(...).compute` takes a parsed `~sheet` instead of a raw string, and cascade-layer handling in `cascade apply`/`cascade diff` is corrected — alongside a large batch of parsing and minification fixes, by [Thomas Gazagnaire](https://github.com/samoht) ([#30524](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30524))
- `yamlx` 0.5.0 adds strict duplicate-key checking on export (`~strict_keys`, raising `Duplicate_key_error`) and a `Value.Build` convenience module for constructing value trees, by [Martin Jambon](https://github.com/mjambon) ([#30520](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30520))
- `obuild` 0.3.0 fixes relative-path compatibility with recent findlib and cstubs/install issues, by [@jeromemaloberti](https://github.com/jeromemaloberti), with the older 0.2.2 release constrained to `ocaml < 5.5` so it stops being selected on newer compilers ([#30522](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30522), [#30541](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30541))
- New packages added this week: `fuse3` (FUSE filesystem bindings) by [Alessandro Strada](https://github.com/astrada) ([#30547](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30547)); `ifs-fractals`, a chaos-game IFS fractal renderer with a CLI and library plus a Fractint-file reader, by [Cédric Bonhomme](https://github.com/cedricbonhomme) ([#30548](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30548)); `ascon`, a dependency-free NIST SP 800-232 Ascon AEAD/hash implementation, by [Ville Vesilehto](https://github.com/thevilledev) ([#30549](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30549)); `locswijch`, a CLI bridging `dune pkg` builds and opam switches for editor tooling, by [Cuihtlauac Alvarado](https://github.com/cuihtlauac) ([#30532](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30532)); `rpmfile`, a pure OCaml RPM file parser, and `bytream`, a streaming bytes I/O library, both by [Михаил](https://github.com/dx3mod) ([#30533](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30533), [#30534](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30534)); and `forcamla`, a formula-driven event-listener library, by [Christopher Sumnicht](https://github.com/thyrgle) ([#30527](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30527))

repositories.discussions_summary: Package archival policy for repos with archived upstreams, and a GC-safety debate on lmdb's C stubs, were the week's notable threads.
repositories.notable_discussions:
- [Dmitrii Kosarev](https://github.com/Kakadu) opened a discussion on **archiving packages whose upstream GitHub repos are already archived** ([#30550](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30550)), listing over a dozen candidates identified via check.ci.ocaml.org and distinguishing packages safe to archive from ones still passing CI despite upstream archival

repositories.brief_summary: Debug-info/DWARF fidelity, runtime heap extensions, and frametable-size work merged alongside a broad wave of newly opened backend and typing PRs.
repositories.new_features_summary: Heap-extension runtime API, reduced frame tables, stack-growth use-after-free fix, and new DWARF/shape-fidelity flags landed this week.
repositories.new_features:
- New runtime API for **heap extensions** ([Nick Barnes](https://github.com/NickBarnes)) adds `caml_add_extent`, letting embedders register externally-allocated memory as valid OCaml blocks the GC can scan ([#6248](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6248))
- **Frame table size** reduced for native code by [Nick Barnes](https://github.com/NickBarnes) through de-duplicated debuginfo strings, a shorter descriptor format, and a bitmap encoding for scannable stack slots ([#6399](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6399))
- Fixed a **stack-growth use-after-free** in `caml_tick_fiber_res` where tick handlers could invalidate the stack pointer during a stack grow, by [Max Slater](https://github.com/TheNumbat) ([#6764](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6764))
- Runtime **atoms** (contentless blocks) now get linker symbols `caml_atom_<N>` so the compiler can reference them directly, by [Nick Barnes](https://github.com/NickBarnes) ([#6779](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6779))
- Backported the **idle-phase major GC** algorithm from upstream OCaml, by [@julesjacobs](https://github.com/julesjacobs); tuning `OCAMLRUNPARAM='o=200,Xsmall_heap_limit=128M'` was measured at roughly 20% aggregate compile-time improvement on a large tree ([#6484](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6484))
- Fixed **fatal errors and incorrect dummy block sizing** when compiling recursive mixed blocks, by [Ryan Tjoa](https://github.com/rtjoa) ([#6844](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6844), [#6843](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6843))
- Default **shape format** flipped to `Debugging_shapes` and debug-info fidelity levels (`low`/`medium`/`high`/`very-high`/`ultra-high`) increased, adding a new `-type-to-shape-max-depth` flag and new `-gupstream-dwarf`/`-gno-upstream-dwarf` flags to restrict DWARF output to upstream-compatible information, by [Simon Spies](https://github.com/spiessimon) ([#5103](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/5103), [#5199](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/5199))
- Fixed `DW_AT_call_{file,line,column}` to report the call site rather than the definition site for inlined calls, by [Kevin Svetlitski](https://github.com/Svetlitski) ([#6877](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6877))
- Added `Cmm.Cname_for_debugger` to name subexpression values for the debugger as part of the ongoing DWARF/Flambda 2 debugging series, by [Mark Shinwell](https://github.com/mshinwell) ([#6513](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6513))
- Preserved debug information for additional pattern matches and cleaned up miscellaneous debug-info handling, by [Simon Spies](https://github.com/spiessimon) ([#6354](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6354), [#6355](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6355))
- Fixed dropped **constructor-local kind bounds** in GADT projections, by [@julesjacobs](https://github.com/julesjacobs) ([#6202](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6202))
- Improved **kind-error diagnostics** for type declarations by attaching provenance to the right-hand side and filtering nested explanations per axis, by [@julesjacobs](https://github.com/julesjacobs) ([#6262](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6262), [#6769](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6769))
- Relaxed the `argument_types_useful` speculative-inlining check so more call sites are considered for inlining, improving compilation speed, by [Basile Clément](https://github.com/bclement-ocp) ([#5760](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/5760))
- Fixed **yielding inference** for `Stdlib.Effect.Shallow.fiber`, by [Aspen Smith](https://github.com/glittershark) ([#6675](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6675))
- Merlin gained **destruct support for unboxed tuples**, by [Liam Stevenson](https://github.com/liam923) ([#6849](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6849)), and can now be built via Nix, also by [Liam Stevenson](https://github.com/liam923)/[Gavin Gray](https://github.com/gavinleroy) ([#6814](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6814))
- Backend fix so never-returning branches are no longer linked to join blocks in `Sub_cfg`, by [Mark Shinwell](https://github.com/mshinwell) ([#6859](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6859)), and `Cfg_merge_blocks` now runs after `Cfg_stack_checks`, by [Xavier Clerc](https://github.com/xclerc) ([#6465](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6465))
- Fixed a typo in the **modes documentation** and corrected the listed identity modalities, by [Stephen Dolan](https://github.com/stedolan) ([#6839](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6839))

repositories.discussions_summary: Bug reports on misleading zero_alloc errors, dune runtest subdirectory failures, and a diagnosed fork_join2 float-correctness issue.
repositories.notable_discussions:
- [Andre Taki](https://github.com/andretaki) reported that `[@zero_alloc]` produces a misleading "called function may allocate" error under dune's dev profile, where the real cause is the `-opaque` flag withholding cross-module information that the checker needs ([#6884](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6884))
- [Andre Taki](https://github.com/andretaki) also reported that `dune runtest` fails with an uncaught `Sys_error` on any project whose expect tests live in a subdirectory, even though the tests themselves pass ([#6883](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6883))
- A pure-function correctness bug reported against `fork_join2` subtasks at `-O2` and above ([#6820](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6820)) was diagnosed by [Xavier Clerc](https://github.com/xclerc) as an `xmm`-register-clobbering issue in `caml_call_realloc_stack_sse`, already fixed by an earlier PR (#6334); [@Bruising6802](https://github.com/Bruising6802) independently confirmed the fix on `main` with a detailed reproduction and register-allocation trace, and also flagged that the `5.4.0-ox2` opam package fails to install due to a stale `ignore-opam.patch`
- [@ievans791](https://github.com/ievans791) filed a tracking issue collecting [Basile Clément](https://github.com/bclement-ocp)'s n-way join fixes as of 2026-08-18 ([#6825](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6825))
- [Basile Clément](https://github.com/bclement-ocp)'s issue revisiting the overly-restrictive `argument_types_useful` speculative-inlining check ([#5150](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/5150)) was closed this week by the corresponding fix ([#5760](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/5760))

repositories.new_features_summary: New zero-copy `Iovec.to_bigarray` API aliases bytes buffers as bigarrays, part of the buffer-type migration in #153.
repositories.new_features:
- Added `Iovec.to_bigarray`, returning a zero-copy `Bigarray.Array1.t` alias over an `Iovec.t`'s underlying `bytes`, letting bigarray-based interfaces interoperate with the library's new bytes-backed buffers without copying, as part of the ongoing **buffer type migration** from bigarray/cstruct to `bytes` ([#153](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring/issues/153), [4116ced](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring/commit/4116ced2ef40a686b0db319595561a3d53ea95ab))
- The implementation introduces a hand-built **bigarray proxy with a GC finaliser chain** on the aliased `bytes` buffer, keeping it alive for as long as any derived bigarray slice remains reachable and preventing the OCaml runtime from freeing `bytes`-backed storage incorrectly ([#153](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring/issues/153), [4116ced](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring/commit/4116ced2ef40a686b0db319595561a3d53ea95ab))
- New internal stub `ocaml_uring_ba_family_refs` tracks how many live bigarrays share a given buffer's proxy, used to decide when the finaliser can safely allow the backing bytes to be collected ([4116ced](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring/commit/4116ced2ef40a686b0db319595561a3d53ea95ab))
- Added aliasing tests in `tests/buffer_test.ml` verifying that writes through the bytes buffer are visible via the bigarray view and vice versa, with bounds checks on the sliced region ([#153](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring/issues/153), [4116ced](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring/commit/4116ced2ef40a686b0db319595561a3d53ea95ab))
repositories.activity_summary: Draft PR #153 migrating buffers from bigarray/cstruct to bytes continued with design and implementation work on safe bigarray aliasing.
repositories.activity:
- [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm)'s draft PR **switching the buffer type to bytes** instead of bigarray/cstruct remains open, with this week's update adding the bigarray-aliasing mechanism described above so existing bigarray-based consumers can still be supported ([#153](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring/issues/153))
- The PR thread captured design input on safely aliasing non-moving `bytes` as a bigarray via a custom proxy and finaliser chain, which [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) then implemented and reported as passing stress testing so far ([#153](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring/issues/153))
repositories.discussions_summary: PR #153 discussion covered a proxy-and-finaliser technique for safely aliasing non-moving bytes as a bigarray.
repositories.notable_discussions: - [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) relayed design feedback from [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) describing a "glorious hack" that aliases non-moving `bytes` as a bigarray via a proxy and finaliser, noting it did not obviously crash under stress testing despite still being evaluated ([#153](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring/issues/153))
repositories.trends_summary: Ongoing shift from bigarray/cstruct to bytes-based buffers is balancing zero-copy interop against OCaml 5 GC lifetime safety.
repositories.emerging_trends:
- Continued effort to reduce the library's dependency on `bigarray`/`cstruct` in favor of plain OCaml `bytes`, while preserving zero-copy interop for bigarray-based consumers through aliasing rather than removing bigarray support outright ([#153](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring/issues/153))
- Buffer-lifetime safety on the OCaml 5 runtime — relying on non-moving `bytes`, GC finalisers, and hand-managed bigarray proxies — is an active design concern shaping the buffer-representation rework ([#153](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring/issues/153))
repositories.contributors_summary: Anil Madhavapeddy advanced the buffer-type migration PR; Thomas Leonard contributed the underlying bigarray-aliasing design.
repositories.contributors:
- [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) continued work on the buffer-type migration PR, implementing the `Iovec.to_bigarray` aliasing mechanism with a custom bigarray proxy and GC finaliser, adding the corresponding stub code and tests, and stress testing the approach ([#153](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring/issues/153))
- [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) contributed the design for safely aliasing non-moving `bytes` as a bigarray, which was relayed and implemented in [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm)'s PR update ([#153](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring/issues/153))

repositories.brief_summary: Eio 1.5 was released with pre-connect socket options and opam availability fixes, plus a new environment-variables API PR opened.
repositories.new_features_summary: Eio 1.5 adds `?bind_to`/`?options` to `Eio.Net.connect` for pre-connect socket configuration, released this week.
repositories.new_features:
- `Eio.Net.connect` gained optional `?bind_to` and `?options` arguments so a socket can be bound to a local address and have `Sockopt.settings` (e.g. `SO_REUSEADDR`, `SO_KEEPALIVE`) applied before connecting, letting multi-homed hosts pick which local address an outbound connection uses; this closes out work started by [@art-w](https://github.com/art-w) ([#713](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/713)) and merged by [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) ([#875](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/875))
- `eio_posix` and `eio_windows` opam files gained `available` constraints so `eio_posix` no longer tries to install on Windows and `eio_windows` only installs on Windows, now that ocaml-ci has Windows support, by [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) ([#921](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/921))
- Released **Eio 1.5** ([#924](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/924)) by [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5), bundling the pre-connect socket options ([#875](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/875)) and opam availability fix ([#921](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/921)) along with previously-landed Windows path support and `Eio.Path.of_dir`; see the [v1.5 release notes](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/releases/tag/v1.5) for the full changelog
repositories.activity_summary: New PRs opened for `Fiber.List.partition_map`, an `Eio.Vars` environment-variable API, and a documentation index, alongside the 1.5 release.
repositories.activity:
- [Kento Okura](https://github.com/kentookura) opened a PR adding `Eio.Fiber.List.partition_map`, noting they could not implement it standalone since `Limiter` is hidden from the interface ([#927](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/927))
- [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) opened a PR adding a curated `index.mld` to replace the hard-to-navigate auto-generated documentation index, with review from [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) on grouping `Eio.Fs` with `Path` and clarifying `Eio_unix`/`Eio_mock` descriptions ([#926](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/926))
- [Patrick Ferris](https://github.com/patricoferris) opened `Eio.Vars.t` on `Stdenv` to expose portable `get`/`put`/`get_all` access to environment variables, following design discussion in [#922](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/922); [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) reviewed extensively, raising thread-safety of `putenv` across domains, an off-by-one in the `A=b` parsing case, missing test coverage, and a future `PATH` parser built on the `Nt_path`/`Posix_path` modules ([#923](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/923))
- [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) merged pre-connect socket options for `Eio.Net.connect`, based on and superseding [@art-w](https://github.com/art-w)'s draft ([#713](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/713), [#875](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/875))
- [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) merged the opam `available` constraints fix ([#921](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/921)) and prepared/merged the 1.5 release ([#924](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/924))
repositories.discussions_summary: Design discussion on a portable `Eio.Vars` environment-variable API, including naming and domain-safety of `putenv`.
repositories.notable_discussions:
- [Patrick Ferris](https://github.com/patricoferris) proposed a portable `System`/environment-variable interface, prompting [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) to suggest `Vars` over `System` to avoid confusion with `Stdenv`, which [Patrick Ferris](https://github.com/patricoferris) adopted when opening the follow-up PR ([#922](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/922), [#923](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/923))
- On the same PR, [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) raised whether `Eio.Vars.put` should be synchronised with a mutex given `putenv` is not thread-safe across domains, and [Patrick Ferris](https://github.com/patricoferris) discussed whether start-of-day usage makes the race window practically significant ([#923](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/923))
- [Thomas Gazagnaire](https://github.com/samoht) requested a capability-safe hard-link primitive (`linkat`-style, taking two dirfds) for use in OCI image extraction, contrasting it with the check-then-use race in flattening paths and calling `Unix.link` directly ([#925](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/925))
- [Thomas Gazagnaire](https://github.com/samoht) reported that `Eio.Private.Trace` allocates 23 words per event once the `runtime_events` ring is active, affecting allocation-profile readings of fiber-dense programs; [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) noted this will be fixed once OCaml 5.6 ships with [ocaml/ocaml#14984](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14984) merged upstream ([#914](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/914))
repositories.trends_summary: Continued focus on cross-platform portability (Windows opam availability) and capability-safe filesystem/network primitives.
repositories.emerging_trends:
- Portability work continues to land in small, targeted increments — opam `available` constraints for Windows this week ([#921](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/921)) following the Windows path support already released in 1.5
- Requests are trending toward closing capability-safety gaps in the filesystem API, exemplified by the hard-link request explicitly modeled on how `~follow:false` closed a similar gap for `chmod` ([#925](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/925))
- New API surface (`Eio.Vars`, `Fiber.List.partition_map`) is being proposed and reviewed with attention to domain-safety and hidden internals like `Limiter`, rather than merged quickly ([#923](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/923), [#927](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/927))
repositories.contributors_summary: Thomas Leonard released 1.5 and improved docs/opam availability; Anil Madhavapeddy merged the socket-options feature and gave detailed API review; others opened new feature and issue proposals.

group_summaries.brief_summary: Security fixes in cohttp, eio and mirage-crypto shipped in opam-repository, while ocaml.org added mdx-tested tutorial code blocks.
group_summaries.new_features_summary: cohttp fixed path traversal, mirage-crypto fixed a timing leak, eio gained Windows paths, and ocaml.org gained mdx-tested tutorials.
group_summaries.new_features:
- **cohttp** 6.3.0 fixes a path-traversal vulnerability in `Cohttp.Path.resolve_local_file` and adds `Cohttp.Path.normalise` for safe access-control checks, by [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) ([ocaml/opam-repository#30528](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30528))
- **mirage-crypto** 2.4.0 fixes a timing leak in elliptic-curve lookup tables (OSEC-2026-17) and a hardcoded Diffie-Hellman group, by [Hannes Mehnert](https://github.com/hannesm) ([ocaml/opam-repository#30507](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30507))
- **eio** 1.5 adds Windows path support to `Eio.Path.t`, pre-connect socket options on `Eio.Net.connect`, and `Eio.Path.of_dir`, by [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) and [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) ([ocaml/opam-repository#30518](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30518))
- **prometheus** 2.0 splits the client into `prometheus-eio` and a cohttp-free `prometheus-reporter`, removing Lwt from the core registry, by [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) ([ocaml/opam-repository#30535](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30535))
- **cascade** 1.1.0 ships breaking CSS-engine changes including stricter `Css.hex` parsing and corrected cascade-layer handling, by [Thomas Gazagnaire](https://github.com/samoht) ([ocaml/opam-repository#30524](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30524))
- New opam packages this week include `fuse3` FUSE bindings by [Alessandro Strada](https://github.com/astrada) ([ocaml/opam-repository#30547](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30547)), `ascon`, a dependency-free NIST Ascon AEAD/hash implementation, by [Ville Vesilehto](https://github.com/thevilledev) ([ocaml/opam-repository#30549](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30549)), and `rpmfile`/`bytream` by [Михаил](https://github.com/dx3mod) ([ocaml/opam-repository#30533](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30533), [ocaml/opam-repository#30534](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30534))
- ocaml.org added **mdx-based automatic testing** of code blocks in tutorials and exercises, wiring a `test_code_examples` Makefile target into CI across 14 tutorials, by [Yassine Haouzane](https://github.com/YassineHaouzane), extended by [Cuihtlauac Alvarado](https://github.com/cuihtlauac) ([ocaml/ocaml.org#3622](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/issues/3622))
- ocaml.org added an **industrial users** entry for Amazon Web Services describing its use of HOL Light to verify the s2n-bignum cryptography project, by [adith nk](https://github.com/adithn875) ([ocaml/ocaml.org#3681](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/issues/3681))
- ocaml.org corrected the **wasm_of_ocaml** tool page to state it targets WebAssembly GC rather than plain WebAssembly, by [Akhil Indurti](https://github.com/smasher164) ([ocaml/ocaml.org#3719](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/issues/3719))
group_summaries.group_overview:
- **Security-driven releases** in [ocaml/opam-repository](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository) dominated the week, with `cohttp` fixing a path-traversal bug and `mirage-crypto` fixing a timing leak, both merged ahead of full CI completion given the security impact ([ocaml/opam-repository#30528](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30528), [ocaml/opam-repository#30507](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30507))
- **OCaml 5.5 compatibility triage** continued at scale in opam-repository, with [Dmitrii Kosarev](https://github.com/Kakadu) adding bounds and depext fixes to over a dozen older packages ([ocaml/opam-repository#30489](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30489), [ocaml/opam-repository#30500](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30500))
- **Package archival policy** was formalised, with several archived-upstream packages marked non-maintained following a triage discussion ([ocaml/opam-repository#30550](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30550))
- **Doc-quality tooling** landed in [ocaml/ocaml.org](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org) via mdx-based testing of tutorial code blocks, which immediately surfaced pre-existing tutorial breakage ([ocaml/ocaml.org#3622](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/issues/3622), [ocaml/ocaml.org#3745](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/issues/3745))
- **OCaml Workshop 2026** content continued incremental build-out on ocaml.org with speaker abstracts and a livestream link ([ocaml/ocaml.org#3742](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/issues/3742), [ocaml/ocaml.org#3749](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/issues/3749))
group_summaries.activity_summary: Dozens of OCaml 5.5 compatibility bounds and archival markings merged in opam-repository; ocaml.org tracked follow-up tutorial fixes.

group_summaries.cross_repository_work:

group_summaries.new_features_summary: opam released 2.6.0~beta1; dune shipped Landlock sandboxing and `dune ocaml inferred-mli`; merlin's destruct now covers let-bindings.
group_summaries.new_features:
- **ocaml/opam** released **2.6.0~beta1** ([Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate), [ocaml/opam#7095](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7095)), bundling switch-list repair on `opam init --reinit` ([ocaml/opam#7068](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7068)), safe-mode cache and debug-level fixes ([ocaml/opam#7067](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7067), [ocaml/opam#7091](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7091)), and disabled git `gc.autoDetach`/`maintenance.autoDetach` on managed repositories to avoid a race with opam's own directory removal ([ocaml/opam#7073](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7073))
- **ocaml/dune** added the `dune ocaml inferred-mli MODULE` command, inferring an interface from a module's actual build configuration and reporting it through `dune promote` ([Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg), [ocaml/dune#16111](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16111))
- **ocaml/dune** confines sandboxed actions on Linux with Landlock ABI 3+, opt-out via `DUNE_CONFIG__LANDLOCK=disabled` ([Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg), [ocaml/dune#15858](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15858))
- **ocaml/dune**: **BREAKING CHANGE** — context names may no longer contain `:`, for Windows/Cygwin path portability ([Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg), [ocaml/dune#16085](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16085))
- **ocaml/dune**: `dune describe workspace` now reports a module `origin` (`source`, `dune`, `ocamllex`/`ocamlyacc`/`menhir`, or `wrapper`), with new `--with-origin-deps` and `--with-origin-deps-expanded` flags ([Nat Karmios](https://github.com/nat-karmios), [ocaml/dune#15478](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15478))
- **ocaml/dune**: `dune pkg lock` now fails without writing a lock directory if any requested platform can't be solved, instead of producing a partial lock ([Ali Caglayan](https://github.com/Alizter), [ocaml/dune#15981](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15981))
- **ocaml/merlin**: the **`destruct` command** can now generate case splits directly on a let-binding's pattern (e.g. `let _ : t = v 1 2`), previously only possible inside match expressions ([Paul-Elliot Anglès d'Auriac](https://github.com/panglesd), [ocaml/merlin#2117](https://github.com/ocaml/merlin/issues/2117))

group_summaries.new_features_summary: Heap-extension runtime API, reduced frame tables, a stack-growth use-after-free fix, and new DWARF/shape-fidelity flags landed in oxcaml/oxcaml.
group_summaries.new_features:
- **[oxcaml/oxcaml](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml)**: new runtime API for **heap extensions** by [Nick Barnes](https://github.com/NickBarnes) adds `caml_add_extent`, letting embedders register externally-allocated memory as valid OCaml blocks the GC can scan ([oxcaml/oxcaml#6248](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6248)).
- **[oxcaml/oxcaml](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml)**: **frame table size** reduced for native code by [Nick Barnes](https://github.com/NickBarnes) through de-duplicated debuginfo strings, a shorter descriptor format, and a bitmap encoding for scannable stack slots ([oxcaml/oxcaml#6399](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6399)).
- **[oxcaml/oxcaml](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml)**: fixed a **stack-growth use-after-free** in `caml_tick_fiber_res` where tick handlers could invalidate the stack pointer during a stack grow, by [Max Slater](https://github.com/TheNumbat) ([oxcaml/oxcaml#6764](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6764)); runtime **atoms** now get linker symbols `caml_atom_<N>`, also by [Nick Barnes](https://github.com/NickBarnes) ([oxcaml/oxcaml#6779](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6779)).
- **[oxcaml/oxcaml](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml)**: backported the **idle-phase major GC** algorithm from upstream OCaml, by [@julesjacobs](https://github.com/julesjacobs); tuning `OCAMLRUNPARAM='o=200,Xsmall_heap_limit=128M'` was measured at roughly 20% aggregate compile-time improvement on a large tree ([oxcaml/oxcaml#6484](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6484)).
- **[oxcaml/oxcaml](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml)**: default **shape format** flipped to `Debugging_shapes` and debug-info fidelity levels increased, adding `-type-to-shape-max-depth` and `-gupstream-dwarf`/`-gno-upstream-dwarf` flags, by [Simon Spies](https://github.com/spiessimon) ([oxcaml/oxcaml#5103](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/5103), [oxcaml/oxcaml#5199](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/5199)); `DW_AT_call_{file,line,column}` now reports the call site rather than the definition site for inlined calls, by [Kevin Svetlitski](https://github.com/Svetlitski) ([oxcaml/oxcaml#6877](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6877)).
- **[oxcaml/oxcaml](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml)**: fixed fatal errors and incorrect dummy block sizing when compiling recursive mixed blocks, by [Ryan Tjoa](https://github.com/rtjoa) ([oxcaml/oxcaml#6844](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6844), [oxcaml/oxcaml#6843](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6843)); Merlin gained **destruct support for unboxed tuples**, by [Liam Stevenson](https://github.com/liam923) ([oxcaml/oxcaml#6849](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6849)), and can now be built via Nix, also by [Liam Stevenson](https://github.com/liam923)/[Gavin Gray](https://github.com/gavinleroy) ([oxcaml/oxcaml#6814](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6814)).

group_summaries.brief_summary: New `Sys.filepath_exists`, native FMA/sqrt codegen for arm64/power/riscv/s390x, and runtime_events corrupt-stream fixes landed in ocaml/ocaml.
group_summaries.new_features_summary: `Sys.filepath_exists` added, bytecode TOC-overflow guard, and native FMA/sqrt/byte-swap instructions across arm64, power, riscv and s390x.
group_summaries.new_features:
- Added `Sys.filepath_exists`, a stricter alternative to `Sys.file_exists` that reports permission and other system errors via a `Sys_error` exception instead of silently returning `false`, and clarified the documentation of `file_exists` to recommend the new function ([ocaml/ocaml#14974](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14974), closing [ocaml/ocaml#12393](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/12393)) by [Khalid](https://github.com/khalidbelk).
- Hardened bytecode executable loading in `caml_read_section_descriptors` against overflow when a corrupted or malicious file declares 2^29 or more table-of-contents entries ([ocaml/ocaml#14872](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14872)) by [Xavier Leroy](https://github.com/xavierleroy).
- `Float.fma` now emits a native fused multiply-add instruction on arm64, power, riscv and s390x instead of calling into C ([ocaml/ocaml#15008](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15008)) by [Zane Hambly](https://github.com/Zaneham).
- The s390x backend now emits `sqdbr` for square root and `lrvgr`/`lrvr` for byte swap natively rather than going through C ([ocaml/ocaml#15002](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15002)) by [Zane Hambly](https://github.com/Zaneham).
- The riscv backend now emits `fsqrt.d` for square root natively ([ocaml/ocaml#15005](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15005)) by [Zane Hambly](https://github.com/Zaneham).
- 32-bit builds now default to and recommend large-file (LFS) and year-2038-safe `time_t` support via `configure`, with `--disable-largefile` and `--disable-year2038` available to opt out ([ocaml/ocaml#14997](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14997)) by [Antonin Décimo](https://github.com/MisterDA).
- Added a cross-backend testsuite check for `sqrt` covering zeros, infinities, NaN, denormals and exact squares, pinning behaviour used by the s390x and riscv sqrt changes ([ocaml/ocaml#15007](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15007)) by [Zane Hambly](https://github.com/Zaneham).
group_summaries.group_overview:
- Activity was concentrated entirely in [ocaml/ocaml](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml) this week; [ocaml/RFCs](https://github.com/ocaml/RFCs) recorded no activity.
- `Sys.filepath_exists` was added as a stricter alternative to `Sys.file_exists` ([ocaml/ocaml#14974](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14974)), and native codegen for FMA, square root and byte swap landed on arm64, power, riscv and s390x ([ocaml/ocaml#15008](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15008), [ocaml/ocaml#15002](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15002), [ocaml/ocaml#15005](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15005)).
- A cluster of `runtime_events` correctness fixes was opened, including two competing fixes for the long-standing "corrupt stream" race ([ocaml/ocaml#15015](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15015), [ocaml/ocaml#15016](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15016)) tracked against [ocaml/ocaml#14151](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14151), and a `lost_words` overflow fix ([ocaml/ocaml#15010](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15010)).
- Five PRs opened this week remain unmerged: native rounding instructions ([ocaml/ocaml#15017](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15017)), the two `runtime_events` corrupt-stream fixes ([ocaml/ocaml#15015](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15015), [ocaml/ocaml#15016](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15016)), the `lost_words` widening ([ocaml/ocaml#15010](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15010)), and physical-equality fast paths for `Set.union`/`inter`/`diff` ([ocaml/ocaml#15009](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15009)).
group_summaries.activity_summary: Five new PRs opened targeting runtime_events corrupt-stream bugs and codegen, alongside ongoing minor-GC and native-atomics review.
group_summaries.activity:
- Five newly opened PRs remain unmerged: native rounding instructions (`Float.round`, `trunc`, `ceil`, `floor`) for arm64 and power ([ocaml/ocaml#15017](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15017)) by [Zane Hambly](https://github.com/Zaneham); a fix for the `runtime_events` "corrupt stream" failure that adds a producer-side memory fence and consumer re-check, with detailed reproduction data across amd64, arm64, riscv64 and ppc64le ([ocaml/ocaml#15016](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15016)) by [Tim McGilchrist](https://github.com/tmcgilchrist); an earlier, narrower fix for the same corrupt-stream issue ([ocaml/ocaml#15015](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15015)) by [Sadiq Jaffer](https://github.com/sadiqj), which the two authors are now discussing combining; widening `lost_words` from `int` to `uint64_t` in the runtime-events lost-events callback to avoid wraparound past `INT_MAX` ([ocaml/ocaml#15010](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15010)) by [Tim McGilchrist](https://github.com/tmcgilchrist); and physical-equality fast paths for `Set.union`, `Set.inter` and `Set.diff` that improve complexity for sets with structural sharing, carried internally at LexiFi for over a decade ([ocaml/ocaml#15009](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15009)) by [Nicolás Ojeda Bär](https://github.com/nojb).
- The `runtime_events` subsystem received concentrated attention beyond the corrupt-stream PRs: a `size_t` fix for ring-buffer file-size overflow past 2 GiB ([ocaml/ocaml#15000](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15000), fixing [ocaml/ocaml#14999](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14999)) and a proposal to expose `EV_C_MAJOR_DIRECT_ALLOCATED_WORDS` and related direct/suspended/resume counters ([ocaml/ocaml#15001](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15001)), both by [Tim McGilchrist](https://github.com/tmcgilchrist), remain open.
- The minor-GC rewrite that inlines the `oldify_one` fast path and upstreams work from OxCaml continues under review, with [Eduardo Souza](https://github.com/udesou) publishing a benchmarking dashboard showing mostly improvements with one workload regression tied to glibc malloc tuning ([ocaml/ocaml#14571](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14571)) by [Nick Barnes](https://github.com/NickBarnes).
- Native atomic exchange and compare-and-set generation across all architectures, follow-up to the fetch-and-add work, remains open for review with a call for extra eyes on the riscv and power fences ([ocaml/ocaml#14980](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14980)) by [Zane Hambly](https://github.com/Zaneham).
- Type-checker cleanup continues in draft form: removing an unnecessary `unify_var` call in `enforce_current_level` ([ocaml/ocaml#14995](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14995)) and making abstract types defined directly in structures injective, a follow-up to [ocaml/ocaml#14982](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14982) and [ocaml/ocaml#14990](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14990) ([ocaml/ocaml#14991](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14991)), both by [Jacques Garrigue](https://github.com/garrigue).
- [Jeremy Yallop](https://github.com/yallop) proposed fixing `Weak.get_copy` so it no longer shallow-duplicates continuations, which can otherwise crash a program with a segmentation fault ([ocaml/ocaml#14988](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14988)).
- Build and CI work continued from [Antonin Décimo](https://github.com/MisterDA): enabling KVM for hardware-accelerated Android emulation in CI, saving roughly 40 seconds per job ([ocaml/ocaml#15003](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15003)), and switching `configure` to Autoconf's own C++ compiler detection to fix a `-std=gnu23` build failure ([ocaml/ocaml#14996](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14996)).
group_summaries.notable_discussions:
- The `runtime_events` "corrupt stream" bug ([ocaml/ocaml#14151](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14151)) prompted parallel investigation: [Sadiq Jaffer](https://github.com/sadiqj) proposed a consumer-side re-check ([ocaml/ocaml#15015](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15015)), while [Tim McGilchrist](https://github.com/tmcgilchrist) traced a second, independent cause — a release-store ordering bug in `write_to_ring` — and added a producer-side fence ([ocaml/ocaml#15016](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15016)); [Zane Hambly](https://github.com/Zaneham) independently reproduced the failure on riscv64 and confirmed the combined fix eliminates it while the consumer-only fix does not.
- Wording for the new `Sys.filepath_exists` and revised `Sys.file_exists` documentation went through several rounds between [Xavier Leroy](https://github.com/xavierleroy), [Daniel Bünzli](https://github.com/dbuenzli) and [Khalid](https://github.com/khalidbelk), settling on plain-language phrasing that avoids POSIX-specific terms like `stat`, `ENOTDIR` and `ENOENT` since `Sys` module readers are not assumed to know POSIX systems programming ([ocaml/ocaml#14974](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14974)).
- [Jeremy Yallop](https://github.com/yallop) found that `Weak.get_copy` shallow-duplicates effect-handler continuations, producing two continuations sharing one fiber and causing a segmentation fault when both are resumed ([ocaml/ocaml#14988](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14988)).
- [Ryan Tjoa](https://github.com/rtjoa) reported that `[%atomic.loc]` on a polymorphic mutable record field can be used to implement `Obj.magic`, an unsoundness hole credited in part to a discussion with Nathan Farlow ([ocaml/ocaml#14987](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14987)).
- Whether `runtime_events` constructor indices should be covered by a maintained wire-format version field was debated by [Gabriel Scherer](https://github.com/gasche), [Sadiq Jaffer](https://github.com/sadiqj), [Tim McGilchrist](https://github.com/tmcgilchrist) and [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm), converging on bumping the version now and enforcing an append-only policy for constructors going forward ([ocaml/ocaml#15011](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15011)).
- Reviewers debated whether the new sharing-based fast paths in `Set.union`/`inter`/`diff` warrant documenting the resulting complexity guarantees, with [Vincent Laviron](https://github.com/lthls) and [Daniel Bünzli](https://github.com/dbuenzli) leaning toward leaving the documentation unchanged since the guarantee is not simple to state precisely ([ocaml/ocaml#15009](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15009)).
- [Vincent Laviron](https://github.com/lthls) found that the ocamldebug wire protocol clamps object headers to 32 bits, which can silently truncate large array sizes during remote debugging, surfaced while investigating support for the Introcaml tool ([ocaml/ocaml#15012](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15012)).
- [Tim McGilchrist](https://github.com/tmcgilchrist) and [Zane Hambly](https://github.com/Zaneham) confirmed the flambda+ThreadSanitizer test combination fails on ppc64le, amd64 Linux and arm64 macOS due to flambda's anonymous-function symbol naming and missing race reports, with McGilchrist taking on the fix ([ocaml/ocaml#15014](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15014)).

group_summaries.new_features:
- **[ocaml-multicore/eio](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio)**: `Eio.Net.connect` gained optional `?bind_to` and `?options` arguments so a socket can be bound to a local address and have `Sockopt.settings` (e.g. `SO_REUSEADDR`, `SO_KEEPALIVE`) applied before connecting, letting multi-homed hosts pick the local address for an outbound connection; built on [@art-w](https://github.com/art-w)'s draft ([ocaml-multicore/eio#713](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/713)) and merged by [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) ([ocaml-multicore/eio#875](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/875))
- **[ocaml-multicore/eio](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio)**: `eio_posix` and `eio_windows` opam files gained `available` constraints so `eio_posix` no longer attempts to install on Windows and vice versa, now that ocaml-ci has Windows support, by [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) ([ocaml-multicore/eio#921](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/921))
- **[ocaml-multicore/eio](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio)**: **Eio 1.5** was released ([ocaml-multicore/eio#924](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/924)) by [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5), bundling the pre-connect socket options, the opam availability fix, and previously-landed Windows path support and `Eio.Path.of_dir` — see the [v1.5 release notes](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/releases/tag/v1.5)
- **[ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring)**: added `Iovec.to_bigarray`, a zero-copy `Bigarray.Array1.t` alias over an `Iovec.t`'s underlying `bytes`, letting bigarray-based interfaces interoperate with the library's new bytes-backed buffers without copying, part of the ongoing buffer-type migration from bigarray/cstruct to `bytes` ([ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#153](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring/issues/153), [4116ced](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring/commit/4116ced2ef40a686b0db319595561a3d53ea95ab))
- **[ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring)**: implementation adds a hand-built bigarray proxy with a GC finaliser chain on the aliased `bytes` buffer, plus a new internal stub `ocaml_uring_ba_family_refs` tracking live bigarray references so the buffer is only freed once all derived views are unreachable, with aliasing tests added in `tests/buffer_test.ml` ([ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#153](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring/issues/153))
