group_summaries.cross_repository_work:
- The same core maintainers were active across both repositories with recorded activity this week: [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) merged the socket-options feature and gave detailed API review in [ocaml-multicore/eio](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio), while also driving the buffer-type migration in [ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring) ([ocaml-multicore/eio#875](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/875), [ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#153](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring/issues/153)); [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) released eio 1.5 ([ocaml-multicore/eio#924](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/924)) and contributed the bigarray-aliasing design used in ocaml-uring's buffer rework ([ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#153](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring/issues/153))
- [ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring) is eio's io_uring backend on Linux, so its buffer-representation rework toward `bytes` ([ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#153](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring/issues/153)) is architecturally related to eio's own I/O buffer handling, though no PR or issue explicitly links the two repositories this week
group_summaries.notable_discussions:
- [Patrick Ferris](https://github.com/patricoferris) proposed a portable `System`/environment-variable interface for eio, prompting [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) to suggest `Vars` over `System` to avoid confusion with `Stdenv`, adopted in the follow-up PR ([ocaml-multicore/eio#922](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/922), [ocaml-multicore/eio#923](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/923))
- On the same PR, [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) raised whether `Eio.Vars.put` should be synchronised with a mutex given `putenv` is not thread-safe across domains, and [Patrick Ferris](https://github.com/patricoferris) discussed whether start-of-day usage makes the race window practically significant ([ocaml-multicore/eio#923](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/923))
- [Thomas Gazagnaire](https://github.com/samoht) requested a capability-safe hard-link primitive (`linkat`-style, taking two dirfds) for use in OCI image extraction, contrasting it with the check-then-use race of flattening paths and calling `Unix.link` directly ([ocaml-multicore/eio#925](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/925))
- [Thomas Gazagnaire](https://github.com/samoht) reported that `Eio.Private.Trace` allocates 23 words per event once the `runtime_events` ring is active, affecting allocation-profile readings of fiber-dense programs; [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) noted this will be fixed once OCaml 5.6 ships with [ocaml/ocaml#14984](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14984) merged upstream ([ocaml-multicore/eio#914](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/914))
- In [ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring), [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) relayed design feedback from [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) describing a technique that aliases non-moving `bytes` as a bigarray via a proxy and finaliser, noting it did not obviously crash under stress testing despite still being evaluated ([ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#153](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring/issues/153))
group_summaries.emerging_trends:
- Portability work continues to land in small, targeted increments in [ocaml-multicore/eio](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio) — opam `available` constraints for Windows this week ([ocaml-multicore/eio#921](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/921)) following the Windows path support already released in 1.5
- Requests are trending toward closing capability-safety gaps in eio's filesystem API, exemplified by the hard-link request explicitly modeled on how `~follow:false` closed a similar gap for `chmod` ([ocaml-multicore/eio#925](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/925))
- New API surface in eio (`Eio.Vars`, `Fiber.List.partition_map`) is being proposed and reviewed with attention to domain-safety and hidden internals like `Limiter`, rather than merged quickly ([ocaml-multicore/eio#923](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/923), [ocaml-multicore/eio#927](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/927))
- Across both active repositories, buffer- and memory-lifetime safety on the OCaml 5 runtime is a shared design concern — eio's per-event trace allocation overhead ([ocaml-multicore/eio#914](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/914)) and ocaml-uring's non-moving `bytes`/GC-finaliser/bigarray-proxy scheme ([ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#153](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring/issues/153)) both hinge on precise control of allocation and object lifetime
- Ongoing shift from `bigarray`/`cstruct` to plain `bytes`-based buffers in ocaml-uring is balancing zero-copy interop against GC lifetime safety rather than dropping bigarray support outright ([ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#153](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring/issues/153))

weekly_summary.brief_summary: Eio 1.5 and opam 2.6.0~beta1 shipped, ocaml/ocaml gained native FMA/sqrt codegen, and opam-repository merged cohttp/mirage-crypto security fixes.
weekly_summary.new_features_summary: Eio 1.5's pre-connect socket options, opam 2.6.0~beta1, dune's Landlock sandboxing, and native FMA/sqrt/byte-swap codegen on four architectures.
weekly_summary.new_features:
- __RUMINANT:multicore__ [ocaml-multicore/eio](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio) released **Eio 1.5** ([ocaml-multicore/eio#924](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/924)), bundling pre-connect socket options on `Eio.Net.connect` via `?bind_to`/`?options` ([ocaml-multicore/eio#875](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/875)) by [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) building on [@art-w](https://github.com/art-w)'s draft, Windows path support, and an opam `available`-constraint fix by [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) ([ocaml-multicore/eio#921](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/921)).
- __RUMINANT:multicore__ [ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring) added `Iovec.to_bigarray`, a zero-copy `Bigarray.Array1.t` alias over the library's new `bytes`-backed buffers, part of its ongoing migration off bigarray/cstruct ([ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#153](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring/issues/153)).
- __RUMINANT:core__ [ocaml/ocaml](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml) added `Sys.filepath_exists`, a stricter alternative to `Sys.file_exists` that reports permission and other system errors via `Sys_error` instead of silently returning `false` ([ocaml/ocaml#14974](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14974)) by [Khalid](https://github.com/khalidbelk).
- __RUMINANT:core__ [ocaml/ocaml](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml) gained native codegen for FMA, square root and byte swap on arm64, power, riscv and s390x instead of C fallbacks, driven by [Zane Hambly](https://github.com/Zaneham) ([ocaml/ocaml#15008](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15008), [ocaml/ocaml#15002](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15002), [ocaml/ocaml#15005](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15005)); 32-bit builds now default to large-file and year-2038-safe `time_t` support ([ocaml/ocaml#14997](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14997)) by [Antonin Décimo](https://github.com/MisterDA).
- __RUMINANT:oxcaml__ [oxcaml/oxcaml](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml) added a runtime API for **heap extensions** (`caml_add_extent`) letting embedders register externally-allocated GC-scannable memory, by [Nick Barnes](https://github.com/NickBarnes) ([oxcaml/oxcaml#6248](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6248)), reduced native-code **frame table size** via de-duplicated debuginfo and bitmap encoding, also by Barnes ([oxcaml/oxcaml#6399](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6399)), and fixed a **stack-growth use-after-free** in `caml_tick_fiber_res` by [Max Slater](https://github.com/TheNumbat) ([oxcaml/oxcaml#6764](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6764)).
- __RUMINANT:oxcaml__ [oxcaml/oxcaml](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml) flipped the default **shape format** to `Debugging_shapes` and added `-gupstream-dwarf` fidelity flags by [Simon Spies](https://github.com/spiessimon) ([oxcaml/oxcaml#5103](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/5103)), and made `DW_AT_call_{file,line,column}` report the call site for inlined calls, by [Kevin Svetlitski](https://github.com/Svetlitski) ([oxcaml/oxcaml#6877](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6877)); Merlin gained **destruct support for unboxed tuples** by [Liam Stevenson](https://github.com/liam923) ([oxcaml/oxcaml#6849](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6849)).
- __RUMINANT:tools__ [ocaml/opam](https://github.com/ocaml/opam) released **2.6.0~beta1** ([ocaml/opam#7095](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7095)) by [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate), bundling switch-list repair on `opam init --reinit` and git `gc.autoDetach`/`maintenance.autoDetach` hardening to avoid a race with opam's own directory removal ([ocaml/opam#7073](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7073)).
- __RUMINANT:tools__ [ocaml/dune](https://github.com/ocaml/dune) added the `dune ocaml inferred-mli MODULE` command ([ocaml/dune#16111](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16111)) and Linux **Landlock sandboxing** for sandboxed actions ([ocaml/dune#15858](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15858)), both by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg); a **breaking change** now disallows `:` in context names for Windows/Cygwin path portability ([ocaml/dune#16085](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16085)).
- __RUMINANT:tools__ [ocaml/merlin](https://github.com/ocaml/merlin)'s `destruct` command can now generate case splits directly on a let-binding's pattern, previously only possible inside match expressions, by [Paul-Elliot Anglès d'Auriac](https://github.com/panglesd) ([ocaml/merlin#2117](https://github.com/ocaml/merlin/issues/2117)).
- __RUMINANT:ecosystem__ [ocaml/opam-repository](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository) merged **cohttp** 6.3.0, fixing a path-traversal vulnerability in `Cohttp.Path.resolve_local_file` ([ocaml/opam-repository#30528](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30528)), and **mirage-crypto** 2.4.0, fixing a timing leak in elliptic-curve lookup tables (OSEC-2026-17) ([ocaml/opam-repository#30507](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30507)), both by [Hannes Mehnert](https://github.com/hannesm) for the latter and [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) for the former.
